input: # divergent.tsv — the inputs where the RUST port answers differently from
# the canonical TypeScript, executed by rs/tests/divergent_test.rs.
#   input  C source. Escapes \n \r \t \\ are decoded, as in test/spec.
#   ts,go,rust
#          what each runtime does: a JSON value, ERROR:<code>, or the
#          literal ABORT, which means the runtime does not return at all
#          — it exhausts its stack and the process dies. ABORT is this
#          file's own vocabulary, defined here, because no error code can
#          stand for "there was no error, there was no answer either".
#   why    the entry in DIVERGENCE.md, and who repairs it.
# NOT A FIXTURE, and NOT IN test/spec. A fixture fails when behaviour
# REGRESSES; this fails BOTH ways. When a port is repaired to agree with
# the others, the row still claims they differ, the suite goes red, and it
# names the row to delete. A divergence recorded as a passing test of
# current behaviour survives its own repair and then describes something
# that no longer happens, with nothing red. It also sits OUTSIDE test/spec
# because both parity runners discover fixtures by listing that directory:
# a register left in there would be run as a fixture by all three runtimes.
# MEASURED 2026-09-21 by running each runtime on each input: the canonical
# under Node over a type-stripped copy of ts/src/c.ts, the Go port through
# a driver binary, and the Rust port through cargo test.
# From 0.6 every runtime builds the canonical's tree with its rules, and
# the ternary and the initializer item that had rows here agree: the
# register holds no row.
# --- 1. Source nested deeper than the realize cap -----------------------
# Not expressible here: the input is thousands of braces, far larger than a
# cell, and the TypeScript and Go answers depend on the stack the process
# happens to have. Pinned by nesting_at_the_cap, nesting_past_the_cap and
# every_recursive_construct_stops_at_the_cap in rs/tests/limits_test.rs,
# and written up in DIVERGENCE.md#1.
